title: Human Dignity and Justice
subtitle: How Islamic ethics guides truthful, compassionate speech about Palestine
summary: Islam commands believers to uphold justice, reject collective blame, and protect people who are not fighting. These Islamic duties can support respect for modern humanitarian law, but the two frameworks are not identical: Quran, Sunnah, and Islamic jurisprudence provide religious guidance, while international humanitarian law supplies modern legal rules for armed conflict.

sections.title: Justice Is an Islamic Obligation
sections.body: Islam does not make justice depend on nationality, faith, or politics. The Quran commands believers to tell the truth even against themselves and to remain just toward people they strongly oppose. These duties give Muslims a clear moral starting point for speaking about Palestinian lives and every innocent life.

sections.title: Justice Even When Emotions Run High
sections.body:
Quran 4:135 commands believers to stand firmly for justice even against themselves, parents, and relatives. Quran 5:8 adds that hatred of a people must not lead to injustice. The full Arabic and English text of both verses appears in the passage cards below.

These commands rule out selective morality. A Muslim may oppose oppression while admitting facts that complicate a preferred narrative, condemning wrongdoing by anyone, and refusing to make an entire people guilty for the actions of a government, army, or armed group. Justice is an act of obedience to Allah.

sections.title: The Prophet Forbade Killing Women and Children
sections.body:
Islamic ethics is not vague about innocent life. In [Sahih al-Bukhari 3015](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3015), the Prophet saw that a woman had been killed during fighting and forbade the killing of women and children. The report establishes an explicit starting rule: women and children who are not taking part in hostilities are not lawful targets. Classical jurists extended protection to other non-fighting people, although they discussed categories and difficult battlefield cases in detail.

This teaching must not be used selectively. Deliberately attacking civilians is wrong whether the victim is Palestinian or Israeli, Muslim, Jewish, Christian, or of no faith. One party's violation does not make revenge against another party's civilians just.

sections.title: Islamic Ethics and Modern Humanitarian Law Are Distinct
sections.body:
Islamic ethical principles come from the Quran, Sunnah, and Islamic jurisprudence. International humanitarian law, or IHL, is a modern legal framework found in treaties and customary rules. They overlap in important protections, but one should not be presented as if it were simply the other. The [ICRC's overview of Islamic law and IHL](https://www.icrc.org/en/law-and-policy/ihl-and-islamic-law) explains both common ground and the need to study each tradition on its own terms.

Under IHL, parties to an armed conflict must distinguish civilians and civilian objects from combatants and military objectives. The law also regulates proportionality and precautions in attack; the [ICRC's rules-of-war guide](https://www.icrc.org/en/document/FAQ-rules-of-war-ihl) gives a beginner-friendly explanation. Applying those rules to a particular event requires reliable facts and legal analysis. A slogan or social-media clip cannot establish a legal judgment by itself.

sections.title: How to Speak and Act Responsibly
sections.body:
Distinguish civilians from governments, armed groups, and political parties. Check a claim's date, place, author, and original evidence. Do not spread unverified figures or images, and do not use suffering as a debate prop.

A faithful response may include prayer, lawful charity through accountable organizations, careful learning, peaceful civic action, and truthful advocacy. It must reject dehumanization, false testimony, deliberate attacks on civilians, and identity-based hatred.

sections.title: Accountability Without Collective Blame
sections.body:
If an armed group attacks civilians, identify the responsible actors and condemn the attack; do not blame an entire population. If credible evidence indicates that state forces violated the law, identify the alleged policy or conduct and rely on competent investigations; do not turn civilians who share a nationality into targets of blame.

This approach is morally serious. It protects the innocent, keeps legal claims tied to evidence, and prevents grief from becoming hatred.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: Human Dignity and Justice
sections.body: Islam requires justice even toward opponents. The Prophet explicitly forbade killing women and children in battle, and jurists extended protection to other non-fighters. Modern humanitarian law adds legal rules of distinction, proportionality, and precautions that must be applied through evidence. In Palestine, faithful concern means defending the oppressed, protecting civilians, rejecting collective blame, and speaking truthfully about every party.

quranVerses.arabic: ۞ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوِ ٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ۚ إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًۭا فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا ۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ وَإِن تَلْوُۥٓا۟ أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًۭا
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation
